findings.failure_path: The record closes the final verification item by pointing to “Local Verification,” but the file ends at line 118 without that section. No current-candidate outcome is given for `make test` or the npm suite, and the profile and landing record give different focused-suite counts. A release reviewer cannot establish which checks passed on the code being landed.
findings.smallest_fix: Add the final candidate identifier, actual commands and outcomes, skips, and residual risks. Label prior counts by revision and provide resolvable references for the cited review and challenge results. Mark any outstanding check pending.

findings.failure_path: When a chunk ends at the end of a nonfinal line range, the comparison stops at `base + end`, but the verified interval extends one byte farther. The adjacent-range test succeeds even though neither body contains the intervening newline. This contradicts the stated guarantee that every separator byte was shown and compared.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep byte-verified intervals bounded by the compared body. If adjacent verified line ranges may establish a boundary from their headers, represent that as a separate line-coverage rule and state the exception in the evidence claim. Retain distinct tests for an inferred range boundary and a missing byte inside a range.

findings.failure_path: Each new conversation starts scanning the directory from the beginning. Once scanning the persistent entries takes longer than the budget, repeated sweeps in the same enumeration order can expire before reaching the same stale shadow every time. Its transcript-derived content can survive further cleanup opportunities indefinitely.
findings.smallest_fix: Give successive bounded sweeps a way to resume or rotate through the remaining entries. Test two budget-limited passes where the eligible shadow lies beyond the first pass, while preserving the exact-name, age, and lock checks.

findings.failure_path: The fresh shadow has no matching `.run.lock`. Even if both age checks are removed, `under_run_lock` fails to open the lock and the fresh content survives. The suite can therefore pass with the stale-only restriction broken. There is also no fresh, exactly named legacy temp under an available lock.
findings.smallest_fix: Give the fresh shadow an unlocked run-lock file and add a fresh legacy temp under that lock. Keep the existing missing-lock case separate. Verify that removing age protection changes the fresh-file assertions.

findings.failure_path: The previous writer serialized one event at a time. The replacement builds every JSON string, joins the entire shadow, then encodes the joined string into another full-size buffer while the event objects are still live. Large transcripts can now exhaust a hook worker’s memory before it returns a verdict.
findings.smallest_fix: Serialize events incrementally to the validated descriptor, retaining it for event-end cleanup. Truncate at the final write position before handing the path to the hook.

findings.failure_path: The generated shell hook interpolates both capture paths without shell quoting. A temporary directory containing spaces breaks the redirection or `cp`, so the inode and privacy test fails before it measures the bridge. The validation record claims fixture-path quoting was fixed.
findings.smallest_fix: Apply `shlex.quote` to the complete `.ids` and capture paths before interpolating them, as the later hardlink fixture already does.

findings.failure_path: The landing plan prescribes an always-on machine-wide rule for subagent use, polling, and review order. None of the frozen bridge acceptance cases depends on that configuration. Including it as a bridge deliverable makes a shared runtime fix appear to require unrelated host-wide behavior changes.
findings.smallest_fix: Split the machine-local rule and its smoke evidence into the separate deliverable the charter identifies. Keep bridge acceptance reproducible with ordinary hook configuration.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The repeated-edit test checks the first denial, later allows, and a separate conversation. Partial-read coverage has one exception to exact byte verification: the bridge credits a separator beyond the end of a returned range.

The initial shadow open refuses symlinks and checks ownership, file type, and link count before writing. Event-end cleanup truncates the held descriptor, which preserves the intended cleanup target across a rename.
Sweep actions recheck age under a nonblocking conversation lock. A budget-limited sweep can repeatedly visit the same directory prefix and leave an eligible interrupted transcript full indefinitely.

The chunk tests distinguish tampering, renumbering, wrong totals, missing chunks, and UTF-8 offset handling. The fresh-shadow fixture cannot detect removal of the age protection because its missing lock file independently prevents cleanup.

The bridge retains the existing full-line parser and recognizes legacy temp names. The new shadow writer increases peak memory on the hook path. The plan also couples bridge acceptance to a separate machine-wide configuration.

The previous writer can replace a persistent shadow on that conversation’s next event. Reverting does not clean interrupted shadows belonging to conversations that never resume. The packet also lacks the final verification record needed for a release decision.

The tests make unsafe-path denials and post-event file state observable. Sweep exhaustion returns silently, so a normal hook verdict gives no indication that an interrupted transcript has repeatedly missed cleanup.

The profile reports 48 passing bridge tests and 12 mutations. The candidate reports 60 tests and a longer mutation walk. These can describe different revisions, but the referenced final verification section is absent. The separator test also proves a narrower property than the source-register claim.

Within the stated private-directory threat model, the descriptor checks address accidental writes through planted links. At the load-evidence boundary, the byte comparison covers each accepted body, while interval extension also records a byte supplied solely by range metadata.

The root contract requires commands, outcomes, skips, and residual risks tied to the current candidate. The plan lists commands and the validation file cites earlier review passes, but the claimed final results and referenced review artifacts cannot be verified from the frozen packet.
